texts.preamble: Praveen Rana vs Devesh Kumar Talan on 12 February, 2026 In The Court Of Dr. Shirish Aggarwal Presiding Officer : Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-01, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Dlnd010038132022 Dar No. 323/22 Sh. Praveen Rana S/o Sh. Dayanand Rana, R/o H.No. Wz-51B, Vashist Park, Gali No. 14, Pankha Road, Sagarpur, New Delhi. ......Claimant/Injured Versus 1. Sh. Devesh Kumar Talan (Driver) S/o Sh. Naresh Pal Singh, R/o H.No. Rz D-24, Dabri Extension, New Delhi. 2. Sh. Naresh Pal Singh (Owner) S/o Late Sh. Chhiddi Singh, R/o H.No. Rz D-24, Dabri Extension, New Delhi. 3. Tata Aig General Insurance Company Ltd. (Insurer) th Registered office at 15 Floor, Tower A, Peninsula Business Park, Ganpatro Kadam Marg, Off Senapati Bapat Marg, Lower Parel, Mumbai.
texts.facts: The present Detailed Accident Report (DAR) for compensation relates to grievous injury suffered by the claimant Sh. Praveen Rana in a road accident that took place on 19.11.2021 at about 9 AM, at Nangal Flyover, Near Shamshan Ghat, Delhi Cantt., New Delhi, regarding which one FIR No.364/21 was registered at PS Delhi Cantt. The offending vehicle involved in this case is a car bearing registration No. DL-9CAJ-2765, which at the relevant time of accident was being driven by respondent no.1 Praveen Rana, owned by respondent no. 2 Naresh Pal and insured with respondent no. 3 TATA AIG General Insurance Company Ltd. Case of the claimant 3. It is the case of the claimant that on 19.11.2021, he was going to his office at Gurugram, Haryana on his bike bearing registration No. DL-9SU-4134. When he reached at Nangal Flyover, near Shamshan Ghat, Delhi Cantt., New Delhi, his bike broke down on the road and he started going back towards the mechanic shop on foot with his bike along side the wall of the flyover. All of a sudden, the offending vehicle bearing registration No. DL-9CAJ-2765, which was being driven by respondent no. 1 at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, came from Delhi Cantt. side and hit his bike due to which he fell down and sustained grievous injuries. It is further stated that the claimant was taken to DDU Hospital where his MLC was prepared by the doctors. Case of respondent no. 1 and 2 4. Respondent no. 1/driver and respondent no. 2/owner did not file their written statement/reply despite opportunity being given. Case of respondent no. 3 5. Respondent no. 3/Insurance Company filed its reply to the DAR wherein it is submitted that the accident took place due to negligence of claimant himself as he was riding his motorcycle on the wrong side of the road and collided with the offending vehicle which was plying on the correct side of the road. It is further submitted that there is an unexplained delay of 15 days in lodging of FIR. It is further submitted that the offending vehicle was duly insured with it in the name of respondent no. 2 w.e.f. 04.01.2021 to 03.01.2022. Issues 6. On 17.05.2023, the following issues were framed by this Tribunal :- 1. OPP. 3. Relief. He tendered his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex. PW1/A and relied upon the following documents :- (i). Ex. PW1/1 is his OPD record and medical bills. (ii). Ex. PW1/2 (OSR) is the copy of ID card issued by the company DCG PAC. (iii). Mark A is the copy of his bank account statement. (iv). Ex. PW1/4 (OSR) is the copy of his Aadhaar card. (v). Ex. PW1/5 (OSR) is the copy of his PAN card. (vi). Ex. PW1/6 is the DAR filed by the IO. 8. The claimant was cross-examined and discharged. Respondents'evidence 9. No witness was examined on behalf by the respondents in rebuttal despite opportunities. Findings 10. 11. The findings on the aforementioned issues are rendered hereinafter in the succeeding paragraphs. Onus to prove this issue was upon the claimant. The claimant deposed as PW1. He deposed that he was going to his office at Gurugram, Haryana on his bike bearing registration No. DL-9SU-4134 and when he reached at Nangal Flyover, near Shamshan Ghat, Delhi Cantt., New Delhi, his bike broke down on the road and he started going back to the mechanic shop on foot with his bike along side the wall of the flyover. He further deposed that suddenly, the offending vehicle bearing registration No. DL-9CAJ-2765, which was being driven by respondent no. 1 at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, came from Delhi Cantt. side and hit his bike due to which he fell down and sustained grievous injuries. Praveen Rana vs Devesh Kumar Talan on 12 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101901024/ 3 13. During cross-examination, the claimant was confronted with the complaint Ex. PW1/R3A in which he had stated that he was going to Gurugram from Sagarpur and was riding his motorcycle on the wrong side as there was a jam on Pankha Road Flyover. After seeing his complaint, the claimant admitted that it bears his signatures, however, he stated that his complete statement was not written by the IO. He further deposed that he was going to Gurugram via Dwarka and as soon as he reached the flyover, his motorcycle broke down and in the process of taking his bike to the mechanic shop, the collision took place with the offending vehicle coming from the front left side. 14. The claimant was also confronted with the mechanical inspection report Ex.PW1/R3B regarding which he stated that he cannot comment upon the same. He admitted that he has not filed any protest petition or complaint to any higher authority giving the correct narration of events.
texts.arguments: He further deposed that he was holding a valid driving license at the time of accident. He further deposed that he has not been challened under Section 184 of the Motor Vehicles Act for driving on the wrong side. 15. The Insurance in its written statement has stated that there is an unexplained delay of 15 days in lodging of FIR. In this regard, reliance is placed upon the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in case Ravi Vs. Badrinarayan, Civil Appeal No. 1926 of 2011 (arising out of S.L.P. (C) No.11974 of 2008), decided on 18.02.2011, wherein it has been held as under :- "......21. The purpose of lodging the FIR in such type of cases is primarily to intimate the police to initiate investigation of criminal offences. Lodging of FIR certainly proves factum of accident so that the victim is able to lodge a case for compensation but delay in doing so cannot be the main ground for rejecting the claim petition. In other words, although lodging of FIR is vital in deciding motor accident claim cases, delay in lodging the same should not be treated as fatal for such proceedings, if claimant has been able to demonstrate satisfactory and cogent reasons for it. Vs. Krishan Pal & Ors., MAC Appeal No. 954/2017, decided on 18.01.2019. 18. Reference in this regard can be made to the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Raj Rani & Ors. Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors. (2009) 13 SCC 654, wherein it was held that the deceased was equally at fault and responsible for the said accident. The relevant observations made in this case are as under:- "17. So for as the issue of "contributory negligence" is concerned, we may notice that the tribunal has deducted 1/3rd from the total compensation on the ground that deceased had contributed to the accident. This court in Usha Rajkhowa and Ors. v. Paramount Industries and Ors. [Civil Appeal No.1088 of 2009 (arising out of SLP (C) No.16647 of 2008)] discussed the issue of contributory negligence noticing, inter alia, earlier decisions on the same topic. It was held that : "20. The question of contributory negligence on the part of the driver in case of collision was considered by this Court in Pramodkumar Rasikbhai Jhaveri v. Karmasey Kunvargi Tak and Ors. reported in (2002) 6 SCC 455. That was also a case of collusion in between a Car and a truck. It was observed in Para 8: 8... The question of contributory negligence arises when there has been some act or omission on the claimant's part, which has materially contributed to the damage caused, and is of such a nature that it may properly be described as `negligence'. Negligence ordinarily means breach of a legal duty to care, but when used in the expression "contributory negligence", it does not mean breach of any duty. It only means the failure by a person to use reasonable care for the safety of either himself or his property, so that he becomes blameworthy in part as an author of his own wrong." The principle of 50:50 in cases of contributory negligence has been discussed and applied in many cases before this court. In Sri Krishna Vishweshwar Hede v. The General Manager, K.S.R.T.C. (2008 ACJ 1617), this court upheld the judgment of the Tribunal assessing the ratio of liability at 50:50 in view of the fact that there was contributory negligence on the part of the appellant and fixed the responsibility for the accident in the ratio of 50:50 on the driver of the bus and the appellant. 19. In this case, the truck was stationary. Some amount of negligence on the part of the deceased cannot be ruled out. Hence in the insistent case, we find that there was contributory negligence on the part of the deceased and accordingly the claimant was entitled to only 50% of the total amount of loss of dependency." 21. In the case of United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Rinki @ Rinku & Ors., MAC Appeal No. 200/2012, decided by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi on 23.07.2012, the following was held :- "8. 22. In the evidence by way of affidavit of claimant, he has deposed that the offending car was being driven at a very high speed, mostly rashly, negligently and without caring for the rules of traffic and thereafter, hit his motorcycle. In the case of Muddasani Venkata Narsaiah (D) Th. Lrs. vs. Muddasani Sarojana AIR 2016 SC 2250, decided by Hon'ble Supreme Court, the following was held :- "16. The effect of non cross-examination is that the statement of witness has not been disputed. The effect of not cross- examining the witnesses has been considered by this Court in Bhoju Mandal & Ors. v. Debnath Bhagat & Ors. AIR 1963 SC 1906. This Court repelled a submission on the ground that same was not put either to the witnesses or suggested before the courts below. Party is required to put his version to the witness. If no such questions are put the court would presume that the witness account has been accepted as held in M/s. Chuni Lal Dwarka Nath v. Hartford Fire Insurance Co. Ltd. & Anr. AIR 1958 Punjab 440." The Hon'ble Apex Court in Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303 has observed that filing of charge sheet against the driver prima facie points towards his complicity in driving the vehicle rashly and negligently. It has been further observed that even when the accused were to be acquitted in the criminal case, the same may be of no effect on the assessment of the liability required in respect of motor accident cases by the Tribunal. Reference in this regard is made to the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court reported as (2009) 13 SC 530 in Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, wherein it has been observed that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular vehicle in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants and the claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability. 27. Having held that the claimant himself was moving on the wrong side of the road, this Tribunal is of the view that there was contributory negligence on the part of claimant. Reference is made to the aforementioned decision in case United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Smt. Rinki, in which also 50% amount was deducted due to contributory negligence. It also stands proved Praveen Rana vs Devesh Kumar Talan on 12 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101901024/ 7 that the car was being driven by respondent no. 1, owned by respondent no. 2 and insured with respondent no. 3. This issue is accordingly decided. The Hon'ble Apex Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343, has laid down heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases as:- Pecuniary damages (Special Damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising : (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General Damages) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
